I Just bought my first "RV" a few months back, its a Lance Squire 8000 truck camper, and fortunately had the good sense to do a couple test runs before planning a big trip. Figured a discussion on the "gotchas" of newb trailer living/camping would be a good place to start off on here. For example, I didn't check my propane and assumed my second tank was full when I bought the unit... it wasn't. Another one, check the fridge out thoroughly before you buy, a replacement is 1.2k+ or about $500 for just the cooling unit, which isn't much fun to change out. What lesson's did you learn the hard way?
I've had pretty good luck with my RVs, but I've found that camping without a reservation can be a big PITA unless you're camping on public land.

So I'll start the introduction with pics from my first trip. Now for the learning part. We were there several days and you can see it's "off grid". I have converted all the malibu energy guzzling stock bulbs to LEDs. Now I can maintain a charge as long as there's some sun every day. The 2 solar panels fold into a suitcase that I DIY. Water is another issue. The park at Arroyo Seco was shown to have water available, so after the fresh tank was getting low, I filled it from the provided spigot near the road using a bucket and funnel set up without first tasting the water!!!! Later that night, after drinking some of the tank water I noticed a funny sulfur smell. Then overnight, I was evacuating my colon repeatedly and glad the bathroom was so close to my bed. My SO did not enjoy the experience either (phew), and we both refer to it as the trip to "Sulfur Springs". Got back, flushed the tank, changed the in-line filter, and will never do that again.

What is a great place to visit that most people don't think of when they pick a vacation destination?
Knysna, South Africa. Tranquil with loads of luxurious resorts without the high end price tag. Plus the dollar is quite strong against the rand making it even cheaper for US and European tourists.
Picture for the lazy. Looks pretty nice!

Heck, any main place in South Africa is amazing; Johannesburg, Cape Town, Knysna, Durban. As a South African, I always encourage people to come visit our country, because we have the most beautiful looking country, an extremely culturally diverse people, lovely weather, and a very rich history.

Some more pros about SA would be that our food and accommodation is very cheap, the most expensive part of your trip would be the cost of your flight.

Stuff to do in Johannesburg: - Take a tour of the Soweto township, visiting a house that Mandela lived in and learning about Apartheid. - Gold Reef City: a theme park built on an old gold mine. - Visit The Cradle of Humankind

Stuff to do in Cape Town: - See Table Mountain - Visit Robyn Island (where Nelson Mandela was imprisoned).

Durban is a great beach holiday destination, and features uShaka marine world (an amazing aquarium) and Gateway (one of the largest malls in South Africa).

I challenge people to come to our country and not fall in love with South Africa.

Kolkata. (Previously known as Calcutta)

Sounds like a joke, but it's a seriously enchanting place- India is in the middle of a remarkable cultural/economic/political transition, and Kolkata is right in the middle of it.

Sure, there's no beaches or palm trees, and the air can be pretty bad, but it's not unpleasant in the winter.

There are all kinds of cool artistic and musical events, a burgeoning foodie scene, beautiful colonial era and Art Deco architecture, and Bengali culture is much more laid-back and friendly than the rest of India. Many people speak at least a bit of English, signs in English are everywhere, things are not as hectic and stressful as elsewhere.

One of the world's great cities, great food, cheap lodging, fascinating history... once you get used to the noise, poverty and dirt, what's not to like?
